resources.string: Halone Test Kit
en-US
Help bring Halone to your glasses

This app records what your glasses report while you follow some short spoken steps. It takes about ten minutes. At the end you get one file to send back to the Halone developers.

It collects: technical details of your phone and glasses, sensor readings while you move your head, the glasses' factory calibration, and your answers. It does not collect your location, contacts, camera, microphone or files. The glasses' serial number is removed from the file.

It only changes a setting on your glasses if you agree when asked.

Nothing is sent anywhere. You choose whether to share the file at the end.

Hi! I\'ll guide you through a few short steps. Keep the phone where you can reach it. When I ask a question, answer on the phone\'s screen.
Ready to start? You can stop at any time.
Plug your glasses into this phone with their cable.
I can\'t find any glasses yet. Are they plugged in?
Yes, they\'re plugged in
Not yet, give me a moment
Found them. Thanks!
I found a device I don\'t recognise. I\'ll record what I can about it.
Waiting for the glasses to show a picture…
Put the glasses on. Can you read big white words on a dark background?
I see the phone\'s screen instead
The phone doesn\'t see the glasses as a screen. What do the glasses show?
Nothing, or black
The phone\'s screen
Something else
If your phone opened a desktop mode, like Samsung DeX, close it. Then we\'ll carry on.
You\'re reading this on your glasses. Answer on the phone.
Now a few display modes. You\'ll change them with the buttons on the glasses, and I\'ll notice when they change.
Using the glasses\' own menu, switch to 3D mode, sometimes called side by side.
Great. Now switch back to the normal 2D mode.
If the glasses\' menu lets you pick a refresh rate, such as 60, 90 or 120 hertz, pick a different one now.
Thanks. Now set the refresh rate back to how it was.
Got it.
No change noticed. Let\'s move on.
I can\'t see the glasses\' display, so I\'ll skip the display modes.
Was anything confusing, or did anything feel wrong? Type it here, or skip.
Nothing to add
That\'s everything. Thank you so much for helping!
Using the buttons on your glasses, open their menu. Set the screen mode to Follow, and turn Stabilizer off. Take your time.
I can\'t find these

Your glasses aren\'t offering their network connection, which I need to read the sensors. It\'s controlled by a TCP/IP setting on their Developer page: double-click X, choose Other, press minus until Serial Number, then hold X for five seconds. Is TCP/IP on there?
It\'s off, or I\'m not sure
It\'s already on
Let\'s try two things. On the Developer page, turn TCP/IP off and then on again. Then unplug the glasses\' cable from the phone, wait a couple of seconds, and plug it back in.
Waiting for the glasses\' network connection: turn TCP/IP off and on again, then unplug the glasses and plug them back in. I\'ll notice when it appears.
It didn\'t work, skip this
I can also look at the glasses\' network setting directly, over the cable. Your phone will ask whether this app may use the glasses. Please tap Allow.
The glasses report their network connection as switched off. I can switch it on for you. It\'s the same setting as TCP/IP, nothing else changes, and I\'ll offer to switch it back at the end. Shall I?
Yes, switch it on
No, leave it
Switching it on. The glasses will disconnect and reconnect by themselves. Leave them plugged in.
Earlier I switched the glasses\' network connection on. Should I switch it back off now?
Switch it back off
Leave it on
Done, it\'s back off.
That didn\'t bring it up. To help us find out why: what version number do the glasses show in their menu, under Other? Type it here, or skip.

Here\'s how to turn it on. Double-click the X button on the glasses to open their menu, and choose Other. Press the minus button until you reach Serial Number. Then hold the X button for five seconds to open the Developer page, and turn TCP/IP on.
Waiting for TCP/IP to be turned on: double-click X, choose Other, press minus until Serial Number, then hold X for five seconds and turn TCP/IP on. I\'ll notice when it\'s on.
I can\'t find it, skip this
That worked, thanks.
Without it I can\'t reach the sensors. That\'s OK, we\'ll carry on with the rest.
One last thing: you turned TCP/IP on for this test. If your phone or TV box had trouble with the glasses before, you can turn it off again the same way.
Your phone will now ask whether this app may use the glasses. Please tap Allow.
Without that permission I can\'t reach the sensors. That\'s OK, we\'ll carry on with the rest.
Connecting to the glasses\' sensors…
I can\'t reach the sensors yet. Let\'s give the glasses a few more seconds.
Still nothing. In the glasses\' menu, is Stabilizer turned off?
Yes, it\'s off
It was on, I\'ve turned it off now
I can\'t find it
Connected to the sensors.
I couldn\'t reach the sensors. That\'s OK, the rest of the test still helps a lot.
Reading the glasses\' factory calibration…
Which glasses are these?
XREAL One Pro
XREAL One
XREAL 1S
Something else
I\'m not sure
Now some head movements. For each one, listen to the whole instruction first, then wait for the beep before you move. Move slowly, and only as far as feels easy.
Take the glasses off and lay them on a table, lenses facing up. Tap Done once they\'re down.
After the beep, don\'t touch the glasses until I speak again.
Put the glasses back on. Tap Done once they\'re on.
After the beep, look straight ahead and keep your head still until I speak again.
After the beep, slowly turn your head to the left, pause, then come back to the middle.
After the beep, slowly turn your head to the right, pause, then come back to the middle.
After the beep, slowly look up, hold it for two seconds, then look back to the middle.
After the beep, slowly look down, hold it for two seconds, then look back to the middle.
After the beep, tilt your head towards your left shoulder, hold it, then come back to the middle.
After the beep, tilt your head towards your right shoulder, hold it, then come back to the middle.
Last one. After the beep, look around the room naturally until I speak again.
I noticed some movement. Let\'s do that one again, keeping completely still.
I didn\'t catch much movement. Let\'s try that one again, a little bigger.
Good.
To be sure I understood your movements, let\'s repeat a couple of them.

Now a few comparisons. You\'ll see green lines on the glasses, fixed in the room around you. I\'ll show two versions, first and second, then ask which looked better. There are no wrong answers. If they look the same, say so.
First
Second
They look the same
For these, look at something in the room straight ahead, under the white cross. After the beep, slowly turn your head left and right.
Which one stayed stuck to the room, instead of sliding as you turned?
For these, after the beep, turn your head quickly from side to side, a few times.
Which one kept up better, without lagging behind or swinging past?
Thank you, that\'s all the comparisons.
The sensors stopped sending data, so I\'ll skip the remaining movements.
